segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby set his jeweler's glasses on the workbench. The cranky, irritable look on the old elf's face was completely gone, replaced by a deep, quiet reverence.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Who are the Unbound?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you ask, brushing the last of the lavender dust from your coat sleeve.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Why didn't that stuff make me forget?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Because you have the spark, child,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby said softly, his voice echoing in the warm cavern.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Centuries ago, when Everfrost was first carved out of the mountain ice, Santa and the Clockmaker realized that Christmas magic was too wild and powerful for any single being to control. Left alone, it would spill into the mortal world and drown everything in an endless holiday. To build the Great Clock and balance the magic, they needed help.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby walked around his workbench and looked up at you.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: They needed humans whose minds were wired differently. Humans born with a rare gift. We called them the Unbound.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip quietly stepped up beside you, his bushy tail stilling. He didn't interrupt. For once, Pip was listening with total, breathless respect.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: In the ordinary world,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby continued gently,

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: an Unbound child often feels out of place. You might look at things and see patterns that other children walk right past. You might understand how things fit together—how machines tick, how people feel, how puzzles connect—almost by pure intuition, even when you can't find the exact words to explain why.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You freeze. A strange warmth spreads through your chest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You think about school. You think about sitting in class, feeling like everyone else had an instruction manual that you were never given. You think about how you always had to hide your thoughts, worried people would think you were strange.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Sometimes,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby said, his kind old eyes meeting yours,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you might have thought that difference was a weakness. Something to be embarrassed about. Something to hide.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The old elf gently reached out and tapped your chest, right over your heart.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It is not a weakness, child. It is the reason the magic cannot touch you. You carry a tiny spark of the original creation inside your mind. You see through the illusions because you see truth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby let out a long, heavy breath.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There hasn't been an Unbound born in your world for over two hundred years. The Clockmaker thought your kind were extinct. He thought no one alive would ever be able to understand the Great Clock's design.
